plumbing.review:
Three changes are needed before merge:

1. **[P1] Preserve deadline errors when reserving incomplete Claude cost.** [claudecode.go:188](claudecode.go:188) discards cancellation information. After an initial provider failure, a paid retry killed by the original deadline therefore becomes an ordinary error: the preservation check in [provider.go:125](provider.go:125) cannot recognize it. Plumbing builds can then check, review and publish leftover files. Preserve the cancellation cause and add coverage for a paid retry interrupted by its deadline; existing incomplete-cost fixtures always supply an explicit connection-reset diagnostic.

2. **[P2] Classify the terminal failure separately from historical stderr.** Both adapters append all stderr to ordinary terminal errors ([codex.go:396](codex.go:396), [claudecode.go:196](claudecode.go:196)). The classifier scans that entire string. An earlier recoverable rate-limit diagnostic followed by a terminal authentication failure consequently triggers provider retries. Prefer the structured terminal failure for classification, retaining stderr for diagnostics, and test this mixed case.

3. **[P2] Include admitted MCP calls in cumulative usage when events are lost.** The trusted counter in [synth.go:212](synth.go:212) enforces the allowance but never contributes to `Usage.ToolCalls`; [provider.go:165](provider.go:165) only sums agent events. The MCP acceptance fixture admits three checks without emitting tool events, yielding an empty usage map. Its [assertions](provider_limits_accept_test.go:120) check enforcement but miss this accounting gap. Reconcile trusted counts without double counting reported events.

Changed files stay within the authorized scope, and all acceptance sources match the ratified plan. I found no production test special-casing, additional sandbox weakening, secret access, or material style mismatch. The new allowance connection is loopback-only. The supplied test report passes; I did not rerun tests in this read-only review.

VERDICT: changes needed — preserve cancellation, distinguish terminal failures from historical diagnostics, and reconcile MCP usage counts, with regression coverage.

usage.summary:
Implemented #261’s retries, shared limits, cumulative usage, conservative cost accounting, saved no-PR failures, and rebuild/review retry behavior. Updated README.md and SPEC.md.

All checks passed on test run 2 of 6: gofmt, go vet, affected package tests, and every acceptance test.

Implementation choice: MCP allowances live in the parent process behind a loopback listener. The merger must record the provider-retry decision, including D-0154’s timeout refinement; `decisions/` was unchanged.
